answer: Israel's Knesset voted 68 to 9 in July 2024 against a Palestinian state west of the Jordan, and in September 2025 Prime Minister Netanyahu said there will be none. Hamas's 2017 document accepts a state on the 1967 lines only as a stage, without recognising Israel or giving up armed struggle. The Palestinian Authority has pledged to disarm Hamas and hold elections, but has held no national election since 2006. Many countries recognised Palestine in 2024-25 and 142 states backed the UN's two-state declaration, yet Gallup finds only 26 percent of Israelis and 32 percent of West Bank and East Jerusalem Palestinians support two states. Our reading: the claim is half right, since Israel is not the only obstacle; two states remain the declared goal of the Palestinian Authority and most of the world, but neither the Israeli government nor Hamas accepts it.

contested.text: Whether a two-state outcome is still physically possible. The case that it is not: Shlaim wrote in 2013 that settlement expansion had shrunk the area available for a Palestinian state 'to the point where a two-state solution is barely conceivable', and in the Palestinian Center's 2018 poll a majority of Palestinians already said it was no longer viable. The case that it is: Peace Now counts about 14 percent of West Bank residents as settlers (2019), the Clinton Parameters would have let Israel keep blocs holding about 80 percent of settlers, and Olmert's 2008 map annexed 4.9 percent of the West Bank. Peace Now also reports that in 2018 more than half of settler population growth was in settlements Israel would probably have to evacuate under the Geneva Initiative's border, which cuts the other way. The card does not choose. Canada's prime minister and Abbas hold that the option is still alive; Shlaim and the Palestinian poll hold that it is not.

contested.text: Whether Palestinian leaders can deliver security. The case that they cannot: Hamas won the 2006 election and took Gaza by force in 2007, Hamas's 2017 document keeps armed struggle and non-recognition, and the Knesset resolution argues that it would be a matter of a short time until Hamas takes over a Palestinian state. The case that they can: Abbas's June 2025 letter commits to disarming Hamas, inviting Arab and international forces and holding elections, France called the pledges unprecedented, and Canada tied its recognition to such commitments. Whether the pledges will be kept is untested.

could_not_verify: Anything after November 2025. The Israeli government's current position after the 2026 election cycle (the party answers on the other card are from a Ynet survey in 2026), any change in the PA's election plans, and the status of Resolution 2803 in 2026 were not verified; this card reflects statements through November 2025.
The text of Hamas's 2017 document itself: we rely on the Guardian, BBC and CFR. The 1988 charter's text and Hamas statements since 7 October 2023 on a state were not read.

The Times of Israel, Reuters and AP pages on the Knesset vote and the UN vote would not load; the UN press release listing the September 2025 recognitions and the Saudi-French joint statement would not load, so the September 2025 recognitions rest on The Guardian, CNN, NBC and a Canadian government page.

Fewer than three reliable sources: the Netanyahu statement (two news pages plus an Israeli government page), the UN General Assembly vote (UN News and the Guardian), the 2024 recognitions (PBS/AP, Al Jazeera and RTE are three news pages but the AP story and Al Jazeera count are close in content).

Which countries recognise Palestine today: the Guardian's count of 147 UN states in September 2025 is before the wave of recognitions that day; we did not find a reliable page giving the post-September total.
The Palestinian Authority's stated position on Israel's right to exist and on payments to prisoners' families: not read, so not stated.
The Israeli-government coalition guidelines and the Likud platform on a Palestinian state were not read; Likud declined to answer Ynet's questionnaire.

Palestinian wrongs the claim's defenders would raise and the card does not carry: that the Palestinian Authority has held no national election since 2006, its payments to prisoners and their families, and its position on recognising Israel as a Jewish state. No page on the card states them; they need new sources. The Palestinian Authority's loss of Gaza to Hamas in 2007 is mentioned on the Ynet, National and Guardian pages cited but is not in any fact's text.

The Knesset's own record: the text of the 18 July 2024 resolution is quoted through NBC's quotation of the Knesset website; the Knesset page and the coalition guidelines of 2022 (the 37th government's guidelines on the right of the Jewish people to the land) could not be read, so Israeli government positions rest on the prime minister's own words as reported by Al Jazeera and NPR and an Israeli foreign ministry page, not the Knesset record.

The Palestinian Authority's prisoner payments: whether the February 2025 decree ended them is disputed between the Authority, Israel and Hamas; we did not find a reliable report of later payments, nor the PA's pre-2025 explanation in its own words, nor the Axios report (page would not load).
The PA's election record has one news source for the postponement (Al Jazeera, citing AFP) and one reference source for the 2006 vote; the 2026 decrees themselves were not read.
not_claimed: Listing who said no to what does not by itself assign blame: a government can refuse for security reasons, domestic politics, or principle, and the card does not rank the refusals.
It does not claim recognition by other countries creates a state, or that the Knesset resolution is law.
It does not claim all Israelis oppose a Palestinian state, or all Palestinians support one; the polls show most on both sides do not currently support the two-state concept.
It does not claim Hamas accepts two states: its 2017 document accepts a state on the 1967 lines as a stage, without recognising Israel.
It does not claim the PA's 2025 pledges have been carried out.

answer_claims.says: Israel's Knesset voted 68 to 9 in July 2024 against a Palestinian state west of the Jordan, and in September 2025 Prime Minister Netanyahu said there will be none.
Hamas's 2017 document accepts a state on the 1967 lines only as a stage, without recognising Israel or giving up armed struggle.
The Palestinian Authority has pledged to disarm Hamas and hold elections, but has held no national election since 2006.

Many countries recognised Palestine in 2024-25 and 142 states backed the UN's two-state declaration, yet Gallup finds only 26 percent of Israelis and 32 percent of West Bank and East Jerusalem Palestinians support two states.

Our reading: the claim is half right, since Israel is not the only obstacle; two states remain the declared goal of the Palestinian Authority and most of the world, but neither the Israeli government nor Hamas accepts it.

skeptic.notes: ROUND 2 (after the writer's rework). Rechecked new and changed facts. Knesset vote (F0): 68 to 9 on the night of 17-18 July 2024 is in Al Jazeera, NBC (quoting the Knesset's website for the text) and CNN; the Knesset's own record was not read. The 25 to 24 preliminary vote of 22 October 2025 (F2) is in Al Jazeera ('Tim Hume and news agencies', agency not named so no wire field can be set; one source). Netanyahu: 18 January 2024 words are in Al Jazeera and the NPR/AP copy; 21 September 2025 statement is the Foreign Ministry's text; 'no Palestinian state' wording exact. Fixed: F3 said Netanyahu 'responded' to Resolution 2803, but NBC dates his words to Sunday 16 November, before the 17 November vote; date and occasion added. Wire: NPR 19 January 2024 is Associated Press copy (marked AP, so F2 counts it once with nothing else AP), Ynet's letter story is by Itamar Eichner and AFP (AFP), Al Jazeera's 10 October 2026 piece is by Al Jazeera staff, AFP and AP (marked AFP, both named on the page), PBS's Abbas piece is AP (AP). F4 (Abbas letter): The National and Ynet report only what the Elysee Palace quoted, so one source; text now says so. F5: no national election since 2006 is stated by Al Jazeera and CFR; 2005 presidential and rule by decree are Al Jazeera's words, attributed. F6 prisoner payments: the same Algemeiner page is cited twice (one site), Al Jazeera is the second; Algemeiner is a pro-Israel outlet and the Israeli Foreign Ministry statement is quoted as that ministry's words. No motive is read into Netanyahu, Abbas or Hamas statements. Round-one removals ('lost Gaza in 2007', 'half right' as a bare verdict) have not come back as claims; 'half right' now sits inside 'Our reading'. Blocking facts (missing sources a person could find): F1 (CNN, NBC; Israeli MFA is government), F2 (Al Jazeera and NPR/AP; the Knesset's record and a second 2025 vote source), F5 (Al Jazeera, CFR; the PA's own election-commission page), F6 (Al Jazeera, Algemeiner; needs a non-Israeli-leaning second source or the Taylor Force Act text), F10 (UN News, Guardian), and F4 which has the count of origins but one underlying source.
